summary: Corrected the catalog grain override for customer_orders to match the dbt model and built data.

findings.claim: The catalog override declared order_id as the grain, but the model groups by customer_id and the schema and manifest identify customer_id as the grain.

evidence.fact: The catalog describes customer_orders as one row per customer and declares customer_id as its grain.
The override previously set the grain to order_id.
The model filters to completed orders and groups by customer_id.
The model schema metadata sets grain to customer_id and tests customer_id for not_null and unique.
The manifest records customer_id in the model metadata and primary_key.

evidence.source: python -c "import duckdb; c=duckdb.connect('../warehouse.duckdb', read_only=True); print('profile', c.execute('select count(*) as rows, count(distinct customer_id) as distinct_customers, count(*) - count(distinct customer_id) as duplicate_customer_rows from main.customer_orders').fetchall())"
evidence.fact: The built relation has 4 rows, 4 distinct customer_id values, and no duplicate customer rows.

action.rationale: Align the catalog override with the SQL grouping, dbt metadata, and bounded uniqueness profile.

changes_made.description: Changed customer_orders.grain from ["order_id"] to ["customer_id"] to match the model grain.
